item.title: uawake 1.0.0-alpha.8
item.description:
Eighth internal alpha (version 1.0.0, build 8): lock and dim. Unsigned. Design and spike results: `docs/LOCK-DIM-DESIGN.md`, `docs/SANDBOX-SPIKE.md`.
### Added - **Lock now**: a popover button, an optional global shortcut (Lock & dim settings) and `uawake://lock`. It turns the display off (`pmset displaysleepnow`, screen saver as fallback); the session keeps running. If your Mac isn't set to ask for a password, or only after a long delay, the button reads "Screen off (no password required)" and links to System Settings › Lock Screen; uawake never says "lock" when it can't lock. - **Auto-lock**: lock after 1–120 idle minutes while a session is active (off by default). - **Dim when idle**: darken every display (20–90 %) after 1–120 idle minutes during a session (off by default). Any input removes it at once. Hidden from screen sharing, screenshots and recordings; the watermark can stay above it; skipped while another app keeps the display awake. - Settings keys `LockShortcutKeyCode`, `LockShortcutModifiers`, `AutoLockEnabled`, `AutoLockMinutes`, `DimEnabled`, `DimMinutes`, `DimDarkness`, `DimKeepsWatermark`, `DimSkipsWhenPlaying` (docs/SETTINGS.md).
### Changed - While the screen is locked, however it was locked, sessions drop their display assertion and keep the system (and on-power) ones; the display assertion returns on unlock.

item.title: uawake 1.0.0-alpha.7
item.description:
Seventh internal alpha (version 1.0.0, build 7): automatic updates. The first build that can update itself; alpha.6 and earlier must be replaced by hand once. Unsigned.
### Added - Automatic updates with Sparkle: uawake checks once a day (on by default) and asks before installing; main window › Updates has "Check for Updates…". Updates are verified with an EdDSA signature. The feed is `https://underscoretec.github.io/uawake/appcast.xml`; archives are the GitHub Release zips. - Acknowledgements in the README.
### Changed - The update channel (`UpdateChannel`) defaults to `beta` while uawake is in pre-release; alphas are published on it. It becomes `stable` with 1.0.
